name: Rust weeps and streaks
kind: weathering effect on gelcoat (surface kind 1), not a surface of its own
code: scripts/make_materials.py, BOAT_CODE, the block starting 'Rust weeps (texture loop, rust lane'

boats.j22: topsides: the hull-deck joint and toe-rail bolts, deck-fitting backing bolts (chainplates, cleats) weep down the hull sides
boats.sunfish: none on the slice (no plain-steel fasteners in the hull sides); the shader still applies if a Sunfish is given Age and Care
boats.berthed fleet: every gelcoat hull with Age and Care (custom data 10 and 11)

slots: any gelcoat slot whose faces are steeper than 45 degrees (|n.z| < 0.7)

levels_needed.L1: none: months old, nothing has had time to bleed (identical to L0 by design)
levels_needed.L2: a couple of short weeps per 2 m, medium strength
levels_needed.L3: ghosts: the old boat's many weeps were cleaned off; faint, long, no dark heads
levels_needed.L4: many long dark weeps, a rust crust at each bolt, a finger splitting off some

drivers: rwN (count and length) = saturate((Age - 1.5) / 12); rwA (strength) = 1 - 0.85 Care; unset Age: 0.5 and 0.8 x the livery's rust channel (Wear.w); salt water x1.5 count, x1.3 strength
replaces: the old 'Rust streaks from fittings' lanes: driven only by the livery's rust channel, so a brand-new (Age 0) club-livery boat carried them and a 20-year neglected one looked the same; thin grey-brown lines that never reached rust colour
maps: none: shader math only, Medium included (no texture reads)
out_of_scope: docks, trailers, dock chain and steel ships use M_WorldSurface, not BOAT_CODE (a later world pass); the hero J/22's baked deck stains (Inputs/j22-hero/j22_materials.py) are unchanged
